formula: rolling_mean(return | volume_change>0) - rolling_mean(return | volume_change<0) over 20 days
code:
def factor_volume_confirmed_conditional_mean_diff(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    vol_change = df_copy["volume"].pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    up_mask = vol_change > 0
    down_mask = vol_change < 0
    up_ret_sum = (ret * up_mask).rolling(20, min_periods=10).sum()
    up_count = up_mask.rolling(20, min_periods=10).sum()
    down_ret_sum = (ret * down_mask).rolling(20, min_periods=10).sum()
    down_count = down_mask.rolling(20, min_periods=10).sum()
    up_mean = up_ret_sum / up_count.replace(0, np.nan)
    down_mean = down_ret_sum / down_count.replace(0, np.nan)
    factor = up_mean - down_mean
    df_copy["factor_volume_confirmed_conditional_mean_diff"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_volume_confirmed_conditional_mean_diff"]
description: This mutation preserves the parent's economic intuition of price-volume coherence but replaces the rolling correlation (dimensionless and direction-agnostic) with a directional conditional mean difference. By computing the average return on volume-expansion days minus average return on volume-contraction days over a trailing 20-day window, the factor captures whether positive price moves are systematically associated with rising volume. A positive value indicates volume-confirmed upward pressure; negative indicates volume-confirmed downward pressure. This is more robust to noise and directly tradable than a correlation, while remaining a single economic mechanism.
